name: Melachot on Yom Tov (Permitted and Prohibited Labors)
notes: The specific labors permitted or prohibited on Yom Tov, including the principle that only food preparation is permitted, and the distinctions from Shabbat

name: Ochel Nefesh (Food Preparation on Yom Tov)
notes: The halakhic principle permitting food-related labors on Yom Tov; the scope and limits of what counts as food preparation

name: Egg Laid on Yom Tov (Nolad)
notes: The specific dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding an egg laid on Yom Tov; the classic case of nolad on Yom Tov

name: Preparation for Yom Tov (Hachanah)
notes: The requirement to prepare items before Yom Tov begins; designation of animals, produce, and other items for Festival use

name: Muktzeh on Yom Tov
notes: Application of muktzeh rules on Yom Tov; items not designated before the Festival such as undomesticated animals, scattered wood, and dead animals

name: Shevut on Yom Tov (Rabbinic Prohibitions)
notes: Rabbinic decrees (shevut) that apply equally on Yom Tov as on Shabbat, including climbing trees, riding animals, clapping, dancing, and various mitzva-related acts

name: Techum on Yom Tov
notes: Travel boundary restrictions on Yom Tov; how they apply to people, animals, vessels, borrowed objects, produce, and water

name: Feet of the Owner (Regel BeAlim / Kedei Raglo)
notes: The principle that objects follow the Shabbat/Yom Tov travel limits of their owner; governs animals, vessels, borrowed items, produce, water, and gifts

name: Disputes of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel
notes: The general phenomenon of halakhic disputes between the schools of Shammai and Hillel; cases where Beit Shammai is lenient and Beit Hillel is strict

name: Semichah (Laying Hands) on Festival Offerings
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether one may lay hands on a peace-offering or burnt-offering brought on a Yom Tov

name: Covering the Blood on Yom Tov
notes: The halakhot of covering blood of slaughtered animals on Yom Tov; dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel about whether earth must be pre-prepared

name: Sending Gifts and Portions on Yom Tov
notes: The halakhot of sending gifts of food and live animals to others on Yom Tov; the dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel

name: Delivering Priestly Gifts on Yom Tov
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel whether challah and other priestly gifts (foreleg, jaw, maw) may be delivered to a priest on Yom Tov

name: Selecting/Sorting (Borer) on Yom Tov
notes: Rules for separating food from refuse (legumes, etc.) on Yom Tov; which tools and methods are permitted

name: Slaughtering Animals on Yom Tov
notes: Rules governing the slaughter of animals on Yom Tov, including the requirement that enough time remain to eat from the animal, and treatment of firstborn animals and animals in danger of dying

name: Hunting and Trapping on Yom Tov
notes: Prohibition of trapping fish, animals, and birds on Yom Tov; rules for taking animals from enclosures (beivarim)

name: Karpef (Enclosed Storage Area)
notes: An enclosed area near a city used for storage; halakhic status regarding handling scattered wood and other muktzeh items on Yom Tov

name: Beivarim (Animal Enclosures)
notes: Enclosures containing animals, fish, or birds; halakhic status of taking from such enclosures on Yom Tov — whether it constitutes hunting

name: Cooking on Yom Tov for Shabbat
notes: The prohibition of cooking on Yom Tov for the following Shabbat without an eruv tavshilin; the institution of eruv tavshilin to permit this

name: Shinui (Performing Actions in an Unusual Manner) on Yom Tov
notes: The principle of performing certain actions on Yom Tov in an unusual manner (shinui) to distinguish them from weekday activities; e.g., pounding spices, sharpening knives, transporting goods

name: Weighing and Measuring on Yom Tov
notes: Prohibition of weighing and measuring in a commercial manner on Yom Tov; permitted alternatives using unconventional methods

name: Domestic vs. Desert Animals on Yom Tov
notes: Distinction between domestic animals (sleeping in city) and desert animals (sleeping in pasture) with respect to slaughter and watering on Yom Tov

name: Insulating Hot Food on Yom Tov
notes: The prohibition of insulating food on Yom Tov for Shabbat ab initio; Rabban Gamliel's stringency in this area

name: Producing Fire on Yom Tov
notes: Prohibition of producing new fire on Yom Tov (from wood, stones, tiles, water vessels); only transferring existing fire is permitted

name: Immersion on Yom Tov and Shabbat
notes: Dispute between Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel regarding immersion of vessels and persons before Yom Tov or on Yom Tov/Shabbat itself

name: Firstborn Animal with Blemish on Festival
notes: Rules for slaughtering a blemished firstborn animal that fell into a cistern on a Festival; whether a blemish must be certified before the Festival

name: Taking Doves from a Dovecote on Yom Tov
notes: Specific rules for taking fledgling doves from a dovecote on Yom Tov; disputes about pre-designation and moving ladders

name: Second Day of Yom Tov (Yom Tov Sheni shel Galuyot)
notes: Implicit context in tractate Beitzah regarding consecutive days of Yom Tov and Shabbat; the institution of the second festival day in the diaspora

name: Kindling Fire on Yom Tov
notes: The dispute whether kindling fire on Yom Tov is permitted for non-food purposes such as heating water for washing feet; Beit Shammai vs. Beit Hillel

name: Animals Transferred Between Domains on Yom Tov
notes: The principle that animals follow the Shabbat limits of their owner; implications for borrowed animals and those given to shepherds
